samples.summary: Apply guard is skipped whenever the popover was opened over a selection (editingHref === null), leaving exactly the #1038 failure it was added to prevent
samples.evidence: `if (editingHref !== null && editor.getLinkAtCursor() !== editingHref)`. `editingHref` is set from `editRequest.initialUrl || null` (line 100), and `initialUrl` is `getLinkAtCursor() ?? ""` (docs-view.tsx:465) — i.e. it is empty, and the guard therefore disabled, for the very common ⌘K-over-a-selection flow. The popover deliberately stays open when the caret/selection changes (lines 80-88), so: select a span → ⌘K → click into the body (which calls `Selection.setRange(null)` and moves the caret) → Apply. `editor.insertLink(url)` then runs with no selection at a caret the user never opened the popover for: either inserting the URL as plain text at the new caret (editor.ts:3679-3686), or — if the caret landed inside *another* hyperlink — taking the new in-place branch (editor.ts:3646) and silently rewriting that link's href *and*, when its label is URL-derived, its display text. That is precisely the "silent edit to a link the user never opened" the comment at lines 50-55 claims to have closed.

samples.summary: The Apply guard compares href *values*, so a caret that moved to a different link with the same URL passes the check and the wrong link is rewritten
samples.evidence: `editor.getLinkAtCursor() !== editingHref` identifies the link by its href string only. A document with two links to the same URL (very common: the same reference linked twice) satisfies the check after the caret has moved from one to the other, so `insertLink` rewrites the second link — including replacing its display text if that text equals the old URL. The stated intent ("the caret can also have moved into a *different* hyperlink") is not met for equal-href links; nothing in `getLinkAtCursor` returns run identity or offsets that could distinguish them.

samples.summary: rewriteLinkHrefInPlace flattens per-sub-run formatting inside the link: the whole URL text takes the style of the run's *last* inline
samples.evidence: When `followsHref` is true the code inserts `url` at `run.end` (so it lands in the run's last inline and inherits *its* style) and then deletes the entire old run text [run.start, run.end). Any style that varied across the run's same-href sub-runs is destroyed — e.g. `[{ 'http', href+bold }, { 's://example.com', href }]` becomes a single non-bold inline. The new test `rewrites the URL text of a link that carries styled sub-runs` (edit-link-in-place.test.ts) sets up exactly this shape but asserts only text and href, so the loss is uncovered. Formatting-only, but it is silent and un-signalled data loss on a path the change makes routine (any ⌘K href edit on a self-labelled link).

samples.summary: The header/footer drag-selection branch bypasses setSnappedRange, so a partially covered link is still reachable there (and rawAnchor is cleared mid-drag)
samples.evidence: `updateDragSelection` returns early for `this.editContext !== 'body'` and writes `this.selection.setRange({ anchor: this.selection.range.anchor, focus: pos })` directly. Every other pointer gesture was routed through `setSnappedRange`, and `insertLink`'s new `linkRunCoveringRange` branch (editor.ts:3612) only recognises a range that covers a link *exactly* — which this path can never produce for a partial drag. So dragging over a link in a header/footer still yields the partial selection #1038 declares unreachable, and ⌘K there falls into the plain `applyInlineStyle` branch, splitting the link and leaving stale display text. `setRange` here also clears `rawAnchor` on every mousemove, so a header/footer drag has no un-snap/raw-anchor semantics at all.

samples.summary: After a snap moves the focus, the caret is given the *pre-snap* hit's lineAffinity, which describes a different offset
samples.evidence: `withOffset` (link-run.ts:183) deliberately drops `lineAffinity` when it changes an endpoint's offset ("dropping a now-stale wrap affinity"), but all three call sites immediately reinstate a stale value: `this.cursor.moveTo(snapped.focus, snapped.focus.lineAffinity ?? result.lineAffinity)` (also lines 2019 and 2075 with `resolved.lineAffinity` / `lineAffinity`). `result.lineAffinity` was computed for the un-snapped offset, so when a snap moves the endpoint across a wrap boundary the caret (and, via the endpoint, the selection painting) can be resolved onto the wrong visual line — the exact staleness `withOffset` exists to remove.

samples.summary: The text-box editor's insertLink selection branch was not given the covering-range in-place rewrite, so #1038 Part A persists there
samples.evidence: `if (selection.hasSelection() && selection.range) { docStore.snapshot(); doc.applyInlineStyle(range, { href: url }); ... }` — no `linkRunCoveringRange` check, unlike editor.ts:3612. A selection that exactly covers a self-labelled link (reachable in the text box by select-all over a link, which the new test file itself performs via `selectAll()`) therefore still ends up with the new href and the old URL as visible text — the stale-label state the caret path immediately below was just fixed to avoid. The two paths in the same file now disagree.

samples.summary: The rewritten selection is always forward, so a backward selection over a link silently flips direction (and loses both endpoints' lineAffinity)
samples.evidence: `const rewritten = { anchor: { ... offset: covered.run.start }, focus: { ... offset: caretOffset } }` is built unconditionally with anchor=start, focus=end, regardless of the direction the user's selection had. A backward drag over a link (anchor at the link end) becomes forward after ⌘K, so a following Shift+Arrow extends from the opposite end from where the user was working.

finding.summary: Apply guard is skipped whenever the popover was opened over a selection (editingHref === null), leaving exactly the #1038 failure it was added to prevent
finding.evidence: `if (editingHref !== null && editor.getLinkAtCursor() !== editingHref)`. `editingHref` is set from `editRequest.initialUrl || null` (line 100), and `initialUrl` is `getLinkAtCursor() ?? ""` (docs-view.tsx:465) — i.e. it is empty, and the guard therefore disabled, for the very common ⌘K-over-a-selection flow. The popover deliberately stays open when the caret/selection changes (lines 80-88), so: select a span → ⌘K → click into the body (which calls `Selection.setRange(null)` and moves the caret) → Apply. `editor.insertLink(url)` then runs with no selection at a caret the user never opened the popover for: either inserting the URL as plain text at the new caret (editor.ts:3679-3686), or — if the caret landed inside *another* hyperlink — taking the new in-place branch (editor.ts:3646) and silently rewriting that link's href *and*, when its label is URL-derived, its display text. That is precisely the "silent edit to a link the user never opened" the comment at lines 50-55 claims to have closed.

verdict.reason: The guard at docs-link-popover.tsx:169 is short-circuited whenever editingHref is null, and editingHref is null exactly when the popover was opened with an empty prefill (line 100: `editRequest.initialUrl || null`), which is what docs-view.tsx:465 produces for ⌘K over a selection or an empty caret (`getLinkAtCursor() ?? ""`). The popover deliberately stays open when the cursor-link changes in edit mode (lines 80-88), and text-editor.ts:1791-1810/1868-1880 shows a body mousedown moves the caret and clears the selection while clicks on the popover's INPUT/BUTTON are ignored — so the "select span → ⌘K → click into body → Apply" path is reachable. Apply then calls editor.insertLink with no selection: editor.ts:3644-3676 rewrites whatever link the caret landed in (href plus URL-derived display text via rewriteLinkHrefInPlace), or editor.ts:3679-3686 inserts the URL as plain text at the unrelated caret. I searched for a counterexample and found none: no outside-click dismissal for this popover in packages/frontend/src/app/docs (only docs-context-menu.tsx:135 and docs-table-context-menu.tsx:112, for other components), no saved-range mechanism for links (only comments/docs-comments-controller.ts:132, for comments), no editor lock while a link request is pending (editor.ts:3774-3778), and no second guard inside insertLink. The popover's own tests at packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/docs-link-popover.test.tsx:127-137 assert the ungated path rather than closing it. Blocking under the correctness lens: wrong behavior on a normal-use path that silently mutates a link the user never opened.

finding.summary: `docStore.snapshot()` is called outside the new `doc.batch(...)`, producing two undo checkpoints for one in-place link edit (and wiping redo on a no-op edit)
finding.evidence: editor.ts:3620 does `docStore.snapshot();` and then, at 3641, `doc.batch(() => {...})`. `MemDocStore.snapshot()` (store/memory.ts:177) pushes an undo checkpoint when `batchDepth === 0`, and `MemDocStore.batch()` (memory.ts:206-209) unconditionally pushes a *second* clone of the same state before running the body. Result: two identical checkpoints for one operation, so the second Cmd+Z (and the first Cmd+Y) appears to do nothing — exactly the failure mode the repo already documents and fixed elsewhere (editor.ts:1218-1222, where `withNamedStyleChange` deliberately puts `docStore.snapshot()` INSIDE `doc.batch`). Worse, when the new URL equals the old href the batch body is a net no-op: `batch()`'s `wroteNothing` path restores `priorRedo` and pops its own checkpoint, but the outer `snapshot()` has already cleared `redoStack` and left a dead undo entry, so re-applying the same URL silently destroys the redo stack. The same pattern is duplicated at packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1202/1212, where the store is always `MemDocStore`. The new test only presses undo once, so it does not catch this.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is not present. In both editors the in-place link edit passes the store snapshot as a callback into `rewriteLinkHrefInPlace` (editor.ts:3614-3616 and 3663-3665; text-box-editor.ts:1205-1207), and that helper invokes `snapshot?.()` INSIDE `doc.batch(...)` (link-run.ts:101-102). `Doc.batch` delegates to `store.batch` (document.ts:146-153), so the callback runs with `MemDocStore.batchDepth > 0`, where `snapshot()` returns early without pushing a checkpoint or clearing redo (memory.ts:177-184). Therefore only one checkpoint is created, and the `wroteNothing` path restores `priorRedo` unharmed (memory.ts:230-236), so a same-URL re-apply does not destroy redo. The reviewer's cited lines are wrong: editor.ts:3620 is `const rewritten = {`, there is no `doc.batch(` at 3641 (3640 is `const pos = cursor.position;`), and text-box-editor.ts:1202-1204 is a comment stating "The snapshot goes inside the batch — see rewriteLinkHrefInPlace" while 1211 is `cursor.moveTo(...)`. All three call sites of the helper were enumerated; none snapshots before the batch.

mergedFrom.summary: Apply silently discards the user's typed URL when the caret has left the link

finding.summary: Apply guard checks only that *some* link is at the caret, so a caret that moved into a different link makes Apply rewrite the wrong link
finding.evidence: `if (editingExistingLink && !editor.getLinkAtCursor()) { … return; }` (docs-link-popover.tsx:152) tests only for the presence of any link at the caret, not that it is the link the popover was opened on (`editUrl`'s original href / `linkInfo.href`). The popover deliberately stays open when the caret leaves the link, so clicking into a *different* hyperlink and pressing Apply passes the guard and `editor.insertLink(url)` takes editor.ts's in-place branch (editor.ts:3617-3667), rewriting the href — and now, with `linkTextFollowsHref` true, the visible text — of a link the user never meant to edit.

verdict.reason: The quoted code does not exist. The Apply guard at docs-link-popover.tsx:169 is `if (editingHref !== null && editor.getLinkAtCursor() !== editingHref)` — an identity comparison against the href the popover was opened on, not the presence-only `editingExistingLink && !editor.getLinkAtCursor()` the finding quotes. The symbol `editingExistingLink` appears nowhere in the repository, and line 152 is `handleRemove`. `editingHref` is set to the opened link's own href on both entry paths (line 100 from editRequest.initialUrl, which docs-view.tsx:465 derives from `editor.getLinkAtCursor()`, and line 142 from `linkInfo.href`), so a caret that moved into a *different* hyperlink fails the comparison and Apply returns with an error message before reaching `editor.insertLink(url)` at line 173. The precise scenario claimed is asserted the opposite way in docs-link-popover.test.tsx:87-97.
